To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the quality of working life of nurses is affected by organizational and personal factors, and (2) nurses’ self-care is a factor that can mitigate the effects of stressful situations.

the main factors affecting the QWL of nurses in stressful situations are related to the type of working hours (shifts, nights, weekends and holidays), and the organizational factors (bureaucracy and lack of communication).
The factors that affect the professional quality of life in the nurses are: the type of working schedule and the working hours (rotating shifts, nights, weekends, holidays and on call).
In summary, our research is concerned with
exploring the variables associated with the quality of life at work and self-care among nursing professionals in stressful situations with high levels of emotional demand.
the quality of life of nurses working under stressful and emotionally demanding situations.
exploring the variables related to work-related quality of life and self-care of nurses who are in situations that are stressful and have high emotional demands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the quality of life of nursing staff in stressful situations and with high emotional demand is affected by organizational factors that hinder the practice of self-care, and that the relationship of help and satisfaction with patients is the main factor that protects the nursing staff in these situations.
the results of this study show that the quality of life of the nurses who participated in the study is not the one they would like it to be.

the quality of life of nurses in situations of high demand is influenced by the organization and the relationship with patients and their families, and that the dimensions of physical, psychological, and social care can attenuate the effects of the situation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it is necessary to deepen the construct of self-care to counteract the emotional problems, to propose intervention strategies, training plans and greater involvement of health institutions to improve the quality of life of nursing.
it is important to know the factors related to the work environment that influence the professional quality of life and the self-care practices of nurses.

the nurses who work in the most critical areas of the health care system, and who have the highest emotional demands, suffer from a poor quality of life at work and from self-care problems, which are related to the physical, psychological and social dimensions of their lives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary to deepen the concept of self-care to counteract the emotional problems of nursing staff.
the quality of life of the nursing staff is affected by their work environment, which in turn affects their health and well-being.
the nurses' quality of life at work is affected by the organizational and professional factors that they experience in their work environment and the way they manage their emotional demands.
